title: Evaluating a Deterministic-Validator Plus Single-Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We evaluate whether a guarded pipeline—single-shot LLM generation followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first-pass misconfiguration on intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under a preregistered paired design (N=300 tasks, cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) using a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic task generation, baseline single-shot generation produced 299/300 valid configurations (99.667%); the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid configurations (100.0%). Paired counts: n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.01], 10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in misconfiguration) is not supported: observed baseline performance was near-ceiling and the runtime sampling semantics recorded in the archived model configuration (temperature = null; generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") increased within-pair correlation and reduced available discordant pairs, limiting the study's power to detect the preregistered effect size. We report the preregistered design, execution counts (planned episodes 600, completed 600, model_calls_used 301), contamination checks (no flagged tasks), and archived validator traces and repair traces. We discuss statistical and operational implications and identify directions for more challenging, adversarial, or multi-model follow-up studies.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configurations is central to intent-driven NetOps, but erroneous or misordered changes can cause outages or security regressions. Prior work proposes verifier- or simulator-in-the-loop and retrieval-augmented designs to reduce factual errors of generative models; architectural recommendations commonly combine generation with deterministic validators and human approval for safer change execution. We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to test whether a frozen deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair call meaningfully reduces first-pass misconfiguration relative to plain single-shot LLM generation on a controlled, paired intent→configuration task set. The research question (preregistered) was: Can a pipeline combining a frozen deterministic configuration validator and a single automated repair iteration reduce the first-pass misconfiguration rate of LLM-generated network configurations relative to plain single-shot generation on a paired intent→configuration task set?
sections.related_work: Recent demonstrations show that LLMs can synthesize configuration templates and translate intent into device configuration artifacts in controlled settings; RAG, verifier-assisted loops, and hybrid deterministic safety nets have been shown to reduce factual errors and improve grounding in domain QA and related tasks. Architectural and survey literature recommend using deterministic validators/simulators (Batfish-style checks, constraint checkers) as safety nets and propose generate→verify→repair workflows for NetOps. However, controlled, preregistered A/B experiments that quantify concrete reduction in misconfiguration rates produced by a minimal guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 repair iteration) are sparse; this gap motivated the present paired confirmatory design.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 deterministic task seeds and two within-task conditions: baseline (single-shot generation) and guarded (same initial generation guarded by a deterministic validator with ≤1 automated repair call). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test: exact McNemar (α=0.05). Model and execution parameters (archived): declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini; the archived model configuration records temperature = null and generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false. We therefore reused the same initial sampled candidate across paired arms for each task (shared_initial_generation stage_count = 300; repair stage_count = 1). Practical implication: the shared-initial-candidate semantics isolate the validator/repair intervention but increase within-pair correlation and reduce discordant pairs for McNemar inference, lowering sensitivity to small absolute differences. Task bank and scoring: 300 synthetic intent→configuration pairs were deterministically generated (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) with canonical reference answers; a frozen deterministic constraint checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) produced pass/fail scores and validator traces. Execution contract limited each task to one initial generation call and at most one repair call; all raw outputs, validator traces, repair prompts, and logs were archived.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned episodes = 600, completed episodes = 600, complete pairs = 300, model_calls_used = 301; no infrastructure/provider failures occurred; contamination checks flagged zero items and no deterministic exclusions/replacements were applied. Primary outcomes (archived analysis artifacts): baseline successes = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded successes = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency table (guarded vs baseline): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333. Bootstrap (paired-percentile) 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair usage: a single repair-stage call occurred and produced the sole discordant correction. Confirmatory-hypothesis interpretation: the preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in misconfiguration) could not be meaningfully evaluated under observed conditions because baseline performance was near-ceiling (299/300), contrary to the preregistration's assumed baseline pass rate used for power planning, and because the shared_initial_candidate runtime semantics (as recorded) reduced the number of potential discordant pairs available to the McNemar test. The McNemar test was executed as planned and reported above, but the design and observed data render the preregistered effect-size detectability unattainable in practice for this run.
sections.discussion: The run demonstrates three operationally relevant points. First, on a constrained, deterministic synthetic task bank and with the tested model/configuration, single-shot LLM generation can achieve near-ceiling validity; in such regimes a simple deterministic validator plus single repair may still fix isolated failures but cannot produce a statistically detectable large relative reduction when headroom is absent. Second, paired designs that reuse an identical initial candidate per pair (shared_initial_candidate) isolate validator effects but increase within-pair correlation and therefore reduce statistical sensitivity to small absolute differences—this interaction between sampling semantics and inference power should be considered during preregistration. Third, validator coverage and task difficulty critically determine observed effect sizes: stronger conclusions about operational safety require harder or adversarial task suites, broader validator coverage (including dynamic emulation), multi-iteration repair, multiple models/sampling regimes (non-null temperature, independent-condition generation), and larger N when baseline pass rates are high. Limitations and operational implication details are summarized below; all per-task traces and artifacts are archived to permit follow-up analyses.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired experiment (N=300) using gpt-5-mini and a frozen deterministic validator with at most one automated repair iteration, baseline single-shot generation was near-ceiling (299/300) and the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs; a single repair call corrected the only observed failure but did not produce a statistically detectable improvement for the preregistered ≥50% relative-reduction hypothesis. The study underscores the need to align preregistered power assumptions and runtime sampling semantics with realistic baseline error rates and shows that deterministic validators can deterministically remedy isolated failures even when baseline outputs are already highly accurate on constrained synthetic tasks. Future confirmatory tests should target more challenging and adversarial task banks, vary sampling semantics, broaden validator fidelity (including emulation), and include multiple model families.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor-template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

Near-ceiling baseline performance (299/300) produced no practical headroom to detect the preregistered target effect (≥50% relative reduction) under the planned design; correlated paired sampling (shared_initial_candidate) further reduced discordant-pair counts and therefore statistical sensitivity.
Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; runtime execution consequences remain unmeasured.
